findings.body: In Ruby the later method definition replaces the earlier one, so the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined at R145-147 is dead code. Any 5-argument caller such as the emoji resize job raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)`, so custom emoji are never downsized and the job crashes.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime ArgumentError in the emoji resize job; the 4-arg downsize API that other code depends on no longer exists.
findings.impact: In Ruby the later method definition replaces the earlier one, so the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined at R145-147 is dead code. Any 5-argument caller such as the emoji resize job raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)`, so custom emoji are never downsized and the job crashes.
findings.root_cause: The patch added a second `def self.downsize` with a different arity without removing or renaming the pre-existing 4-arg definition it silently overrides.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove one of the two definitions; e.g. keep a single `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` and update `resize_emoji.rb` to pass "100x100", or give the new dimension-string variant a distinct name (e.g. `downsize_to`).
findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition shadows the 4-arg variant, breaking existing 5-argument callers
findings.trigger: The ResizeEmoji job runs and calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14), which passes 5 arguments.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds duplicate `def self.downsize` at R149-151 which shadows the 4-arg version at R145-147. Repository context confirms `resize_emoji.rb:14` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 args, which will fail with ArgumentError since the later 3-arg definition replaces the earlier one.

findings.body: The client validation no longer matches server enforcement: attachments up to 10MB pass client validation, are fully uploaded, then rejected by `Validators::UploadValidator` (which still uses `SiteSetting.max_#{type}_size_kb`), wasting bandwidth and showing a late/confusing error; conversely files above 10MB are rejected client-side even when the admin configured a larger limit. Existing JS tests that set `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` (test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:55,79) now exercise dead configuration and will fail.
findings.failure_mode: Client/server validation divergence: uploads pass the client check but fail server validation (or vice versa), and existing tests break.
findings.impact: The client validation no longer matches server enforcement: attachments up to 10MB pass client validation, are fully uploaded, then rejected by `Validators::UploadValidator` (which still uses `SiteSetting.max_#{type}_size_kb`), wasting bandwidth and showing a late/confusing error; conversely files above 10MB are rejected client-side even when the admin configured a larger limit. Existing JS tests that set `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` (test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:55,79) now exercise dead configuration and will fail.
findings.root_cause: The site-setting lookup was replaced with a hardcoded 10240 kB constant applied to both images and attachments.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep reading the per-type setting (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`); if images should be allowed to exceed it for auto-downsizing, only relax the check for `type === 'image'` rather than hardcoding 10MB for all types.
findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcodes 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb site settings
findings.trigger: An admin configures `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 3072 kB) or `max_image_size_kb` to a value other than 10240 kB, and a user uploads a file between the configured limit and 10MB (or above 10MB when the admin allowed larger uploads).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch at R182 replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Repository context shows server validator at `lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81` still uses `SiteSetting.send("max_#{type}_size_kb")`, causing client/server validation divergence.

raw_findings.body: The user is told the maximum size is 10240 kB even when the real server/webserver limit differs (default 3072 kB), giving misleading guidance about what size will succeed.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` (or the appropriate per-type setting) as the value interpolated into the `file_too_large` message.
raw_findings.title: 413 error alert reports hardcoded 10MB instead of the actual configured limit
raw_findings.trigger: The web server (nginx `client_max_body_size`, per the setting's own documentation) rejects an upload with HTTP 413; the displayed limit is derived from this hardcoded constant instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`.

raw_findings.body: The download is silently truncated at ~10MB regardless of the admin-configured limit, producing a corrupt/partial file that then fails image parsing or produces a broken upload, with no way for admins to raise the cap via settings.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silently truncated downloads and admin configuration that no longer takes effect.
raw_findings.impact: The download is silently truncated at ~10MB regardless of the admin-configured limit, producing a corrupt/partial file that then fails image parsing or produces a broken upload, with no way for admins to raise the cap via settings.
raw_findings.root_cause: A configurable setting-based limit was replaced with a hardcoded 10.megabytes magic number.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Derive the cap from settings, e.g. `[SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb].max.kilobytes` (the pattern already used in upload.rb:169 and lib/file_store/base_store.rb:61), possibly with a headroom factor for the downsizing feature.
raw_findings.title: API URL download cap hardcoded to 10.megabytes, ignoring the configured max_image_size_kb
raw_findings.trigger: An API client provides a `url` pointing at a file larger than 10MB while the admin has configured `max_image_size_kb` (or attachment limits) above 10240 kB; `FileHelper.download` stops writing once the file exceeds `max_file_size`.

raw_findings.body: gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions, not a percentage, so the command fails; `convert_with` returns false, the loop uselessly retries the failing command 5 times, the GIF is never shrunk, and the upload is then rejected by the size validator despite the feature promising automatic downsizing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Automatic downsizing silently fails for oversized animated GIFs; the upload is rejected after 5 wasted subprocess invocations.
raw_findings.impact: gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions, not a percentage, so the command fails; `convert_with` returns false, the loop uselessly retries the failing command 5 times, the GIF is never shrunk, and the upload is then rejected by the size validator despite the feature promising automatic downsizing.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new downsize loop passes a percentage geometry string into a code path whose animated branch delegates to gifsicle, which only accepts absolute dimensions.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute pixel dimensions before calling downsize (e.g. read the image size and pass an "WxH" string), or use gifsicle's `--scale 0.8` for the animated path when a percentage is requested.
raw_findings.title: Percentage geometry "80%" is passed to gifsicle's --resize-fit for animated GIFs, which does not accept percentages
raw_findings.trigger: A user uploads a `.gif` larger than `max_image_size_kb` while `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled; `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%` (optimized_image.rb R137-139, R120).

raw_findings.body: ImageMagick rewriting an SVG in place can corrupt or lossily re-encode the vector file (and rarely reduces its byte size), whereas `Upload.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG (upload.rb L63) and `OptimizedImage.create_for` copies SVGs untouched (optimized_image.rb L45-46). Users may end up with a mangled SVG stored, or 5 futile convert invocations followed by validator rejection.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Raster conversion applied to a vector format in place, risking data corruption of the stored upload.
raw_findings.impact: ImageMagick rewriting an SVG in place can corrupt or lossily re-encode the vector file (and rarely reduces its byte size), whereas `Upload.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG (upload.rb L63) and `OptimizedImage.create_for` copies SVGs untouched (optimized_image.rb L45-46). Users may end up with a mangled SVG stored, or 5 futile convert invocations followed by validator rejection.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new guard uses `FileHelper.is_image?`, which includes SVG, unlike the rest of the codebase that treats SVG as non-resizable.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Exclude SVG from the downsize loop, e.g. add `&& filename !~ /\.svg$/i` mirroring the existing SVG special-casing.
raw_findings.title: Auto-downsize loop runs ImageMagick convert in place on SVG uploads
raw_findings.trigger: A user uploads a `.svg` file larger than `max_image_size_kb`; `FileHelper.is_image?` matches svg (file_helper.rb L31), so the loop runs `convert file.svg ... file.svg` on the vector source.

raw_findings.body: The loop's boundary conditions (max_image_size_kb == 0, non-image files, downsize failure exhausting 5 attempts, the new 3-arg downsize signature) are unverified; regressions such as the duplicate-downsize ArgumentError would not be caught before merge.
raw_findings.evidence:
if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)
        attempt = 5
        while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes
          OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)
          attempt -= 1
        end
      end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested feature path; defects in the loop or the API change ship silently.
raw_findings.impact: The loop's boundary conditions (max_image_size_kb == 0, non-image files, downsize failure exhausting 5 attempts, the new 3-arg downsize signature) are unverified; regressions such as the duplicate-downsize ArgumentError would not be caught before merge.
raw_findings.root_cause: New behavior with multiple guard conditions and a changed public method signature was introduced without any accompanying tests.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add controller/model specs covering: an oversized image is downsized until under the limit, a non-image and an image with max_image_size_kb=0 are left untouched, and the loop terminates after 5 failed attempts; also add a spec asserting the new `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` signature.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for the new automatic image downsizing path in create_upload
raw_findings.trigger: Review of the patch: it adds a headline feature ("automatically downsize large images") including a bounded retry loop, a settings guard, and a signature change to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but a repository search for `downsize` under spec/ returns no matches and the patch adds no spec.

validated_findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcodes 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb site settings
validated_findings.trigger: An admin configures `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 3072 kB) or `max_image_size_kb` to a value other than 10240 kB, and a user uploads a file between the configured limit and 10MB (or above 10MB when the admin allowed larger uploads).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch at R182 replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Repository context shows server validator at `lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81` still uses `SiteSetting.send("max_#{type}_size_kb")`, causing client/server validation divergence.

validated_findings.body: The user is told the maximum size is 10240 kB even when the real server/webserver limit differs (default 3072 kB), giving misleading guidance about what size will succeed.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect user-facing error message that does not reflect the effective limit.
validated_findings.impact: The user is told the maximum size is 10240 kB even when the real server/webserver limit differs (default 3072 kB), giving misleading guidance about what size will succeed.
validated_findings.root_cause: The setting lookup in the 413 error handler was replaced with a hardcoded 10*1024 constant.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` (or the appropriate per-type setting) as the value interpolated into the `file_too_large` message.
validated_findings.title: 413 error alert reports hardcoded 10MB instead of the actual configured limit
validated_findings.trigger: The web server (nginx `client_max_body_size`, per the setting's own documentation) rejects an upload with HTTP 413; the displayed limit is derived from this hardcoded constant instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same root cause as candidate 1: hardcoded 10MB replacing site setting lookup. Both are in utilities.js, same causal defect (hardcoded constant ignoring settings), same fix needed. Line 246 is the 413 error handler variant of the same issue.

validated_findings.body: The download is silently truncated at ~10MB regardless of the admin-configured limit, producing a corrupt/partial file that then fails image parsing or produces a broken upload, with no way for admins to raise the cap via settings.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silently truncated downloads and admin configuration that no longer takes effect.
validated_findings.impact: The download is silently truncated at ~10MB regardless of the admin-configured limit, producing a corrupt/partial file that then fails image parsing or produces a broken upload, with no way for admins to raise the cap via settings.
validated_findings.root_cause: A configurable setting-based limit was replaced with a hardcoded 10.megabytes magic number.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Derive the cap from settings, e.g. `[SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb].max.kilobytes` (the pattern already used in upload.rb:169 and lib/file_store/base_store.rb:61), possibly with a headroom factor for the downsizing feature.
validated_findings.title: API URL download cap hardcoded to 10.megabytes, ignoring the configured max_image_size_kb
validated_findings.trigger: An API client provides a `url` pointing at a file larger than 10MB while the admin has configured `max_image_size_kb` (or attachment limits) above 10240 kB; `FileHelper.download` stops writing once the file exceeds `max_file_size`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch at R55 replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with hardcoded `10.megabytes` for API URL downloads. This is a distinct code path (server-side download cap) from the client-side validation in candidates 1-2, requiring a separate fix.

validated_findings.body: gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions, not a percentage, so the command fails; `convert_with` returns false, the loop uselessly retries the failing command 5 times, the GIF is never shrunk, and the upload is then rejected by the size validator despite the feature promising automatic downsizing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Automatic downsizing silently fails for oversized animated GIFs; the upload is rejected after 5 wasted subprocess invocations.
validated_findings.impact: gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions, not a percentage, so the command fails; `convert_with` returns false, the loop uselessly retries the failing command 5 times, the GIF is never shrunk, and the upload is then rejected by the size validator despite the feature promising automatic downsizing.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new downsize loop passes a percentage geometry string into a code path whose animated branch delegates to gifsicle, which only accepts absolute dimensions.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute pixel dimensions before calling downsize (e.g. read the image size and pass an "WxH" string), or use gifsicle's `--scale 0.8` for the animated path when a percentage is requested.
validated_findings.title: Percentage geometry "80%" is passed to gifsicle's --resize-fit for animated GIFs, which does not accept percentages
validated_findings.trigger: A user uploads a `.gif` larger than `max_image_size_kb` while `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled; `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%` (optimized_image.rb R137-139, R120).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch at R67 passes "80%" to `OptimizedImage.downsize`. Repository context shows `downsize_instructions_animated` at L137-138 delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` which uses `--resize-fit #{dimensions}` for gifsicle. gifsicle's --resize-fit does not accept percentage strings, only WxH dimensions.

validated_findings.body: ImageMagick rewriting an SVG in place can corrupt or lossily re-encode the vector file (and rarely reduces its byte size), whereas `Upload.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG (upload.rb L63) and `OptimizedImage.create_for` copies SVGs untouched (optimized_image.rb L45-46). Users may end up with a mangled SVG stored, or 5 futile convert invocations followed by validator rejection.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Raster conversion applied to a vector format in place, risking data corruption of the stored upload.
validated_findings.impact: ImageMagick rewriting an SVG in place can corrupt or lossily re-encode the vector file (and rarely reduces its byte size), whereas `Upload.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG (upload.rb L63) and `OptimizedImage.create_for` copies SVGs untouched (optimized_image.rb L45-46). Users may end up with a mangled SVG stored, or 5 futile convert invocations followed by validator rejection.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new guard uses `FileHelper.is_image?`, which includes SVG, unlike the rest of the codebase that treats SVG as non-resizable.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Exclude SVG from the downsize loop, e.g. add `&& filename !~ /\.svg$/i` mirroring the existing SVG special-casing.
validated_findings.title: Auto-downsize loop runs ImageMagick convert in place on SVG uploads
validated_findings.trigger: A user uploads a `.svg` file larger than `max_image_size_kb`; `FileHelper.is_image?` matches svg (file_helper.rb L31), so the loop runs `convert file.svg ... file.svg` on the vector source.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch at R64 uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` which per `lib/file_helper.rb:31` includes 'svg'. The downsize loop would run ImageMagick convert on SVG files, while `optimized_image.rb:45-46` explicitly copies SVGs untouched, indicating SVGs should be excluded from resize operations.

validated_findings.body: The loop's boundary conditions (max_image_size_kb == 0, non-image files, downsize failure exhausting 5 attempts, the new 3-arg downsize signature) are unverified; regressions such as the duplicate-downsize ArgumentError would not be caught before merge.
validated_findings.evidence:
if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)
        attempt = 5
        while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes
          OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)
          attempt -= 1
        end
      end
validated_findings.failure_mode: Untested feature path; defects in the loop or the API change ship silently.
validated_findings.impact: The loop's boundary conditions (max_image_size_kb == 0, non-image files, downsize failure exhausting 5 attempts, the new 3-arg downsize signature) are unverified; regressions such as the duplicate-downsize ArgumentError would not be caught before merge.
validated_findings.root_cause: New behavior with multiple guard conditions and a changed public method signature was introduced without any accompanying tests.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add controller/model specs covering: an oversized image is downsized until under the limit, a non-image and an image with max_image_size_kb=0 are left untouched, and the loop terminates after 5 failed attempts; also add a spec asserting the new `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` signature.
validated_findings.title: No test coverage for the new automatic image downsizing path in create_upload
validated_findings.trigger: Review of the patch: it adds a headline feature ("automatically downsize large images") including a bounded retry loop, a settings guard, and a signature change to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but a repository search for `downsize` under spec/ returns no matches and the patch adds no spec.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test gap observation, not a concrete defect. The claim about missing tests is valid but test coverage gaps are stylistic/process issues, not bugs introduced by the patch with concrete runtime impact.
